videos.script: Somebody asks which model sent last month's vouchers. And whether it can be built again. {{ask}} Lesson 5's record can name the data. It cannot name the code, and it cannot say which of five models made it to production. {{record}} A model is four things at once. The code that trained it, the data it read, the settings it was given, and the libraries it ran on. A version has to name all four. {{four}} Git keeps the code. DVC keeps the data and the files the pipeline makes, in a store of its own, with a small pointer file in Git. MLflow keeps every training run, its scores, and a registry of models with names that people can point at. {{tools}} This lesson puts the pipeline under all three. DVC runs it, and runs it again doing nothing, because nothing changed. {{repro}} Then a change to one line. The ranking stays the same. The probabilities more than double. {{change}} The registry keeps both versions, and the alias champion stays where it was. {{alias}} And then the step back. One checkout, and the old model and its data are on disk again, byte for byte. {{back}}
